questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question: Which scientist first saw and described a live cell?

solution.key_concept: Historical milestones in the discovery of the cell.
steps: Anton von Leeuwenhoek was the first to see and describe a live cell.
Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus.
Schleiden and Virchow made later contributions to cell theory.
solution.why_not_others: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus. Schleiden studied plant cells and co-proposed cell theory. Virchow proposed Omnis cellula-e cellula.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the discoverer of the nucleus (Robert Brown) with the first observer of a live cell.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question: The cell theory proposed by Schleiden and Schwann was incomplete. Which aspect did it fail to explain, which Rudolf Virchow later supplied?
options: That all plants are composed of different kinds of cells
That animal cells have a thin outer layer, the plasma membrane
That the cell wall is unique to plant cells

solution.key_concept: Virchow's modification of cell theory.
steps: Schleiden and Schwann's cell theory did not explain how new cells form.
In 1855 Virchow stated that new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).
His addition completed the theory.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): How new cells are formed
solution.why_not_others: Options 1-3 were observations made by Schleiden and Schwann themselves, so they were already part of the original theory.
solution.common_trap: Picking one of Schleiden's or Schwann's own observations as the missing part.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question: Which of the following was reported by Theodore Schwann?
options: Cells have a thin outer layer, now called the plasma membrane, and the cell wall is unique to plant cells
All plants are made of different kinds of cells that form tissues
New cells arise from pre-existing cells

solution.key_concept: Matching scientists to their contributions to cell biology.
steps: Schwann (1839) studied animal cells.
He reported a thin outer layer (the plasma membrane) in animal cells.
He also concluded that the cell wall is unique to plant cells.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Cells have a thin outer layer, now called the plasma membrane, and the cell wall is unique to plant cells
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 is Schleiden's observation (1838). Option 3 is Virchow's (1855). The nucleus was discovered by Robert Brown.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up Schleiden (plants) with Schwann (animals).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of life, and anything less than a complete cell cannot live independently.
statements.R: The cell theory of Schleiden and Schwann explained that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Scope of the original cell theory versus Virchow's contribution.
steps: The cell is the basic unit of life, and less than a complete cell cannot live independently. A is true.
Schleiden and Schwann's theory did not explain how new cells form.
That idea came from Virchow in 1855, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options 1, 2 and 4 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Crediting Omnis cellula-e cellula to Schleiden and Schwann instead of Virchow.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Schleiden's observations (1838) were made on plants, whereas Schwann's (1839) were made on animal cells.
statements.II: Modern cell theory states that all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells, and that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Chronology of cell theory and the two tenets of modern cell theory.
steps: Schleiden, a botanist, worked on plants in 1838. Schwann, a zoologist, worked on animal cells in 1839. Statement I is correct.
Modern cell theory has two tenets: organisms are made of cells and products of cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells. Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so any option marking either one as incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the years or the organisms studied by Schleiden and Schwann, or forgetting 'products of cells'.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; plant and animal cells
questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a eukaryote?

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing prokaryotes from eukaryotes.
steps: Prokaryotes are bacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma and PPLO.
Eukaryotes include protists, fungi, plants and animals.
So a fungus is the eukaryote.
solution.why_not_others: Mycoplasma, cyanobacteria and PPLO all lack a membrane-bound nucleus, so they are prokaryotes.
solution.common_trap: Calling fungi prokaryotes because they are microscopic or simple.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; plant and animal cells
questions.question: A prokaryotic ribosome is made of a 50S and a 30S subunit. What is the sedimentation coefficient of the complete ribosome?

solution.key_concept: Svedberg units are not additive.
steps: The S value depends on sedimentation rate, which depends on size and shape.
So subunit S values cannot simply be added together.
The prokaryotic ribosome (50S + 30S) is 70S.
solution.why_not_others: 80S comes from adding the S values, and it is also the eukaryotic ribosome. 20S comes from subtracting them. 60S is a eukaryotic large subunit.
solution.common_trap: Adding 50S and 30S to get 80S.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; plant and animal cells
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a cell with its approximate size?

solution.key_concept: Cell size varies widely.
steps: Mycoplasma is the smallest cell, about $0.3\ \mu m$.
Bacteria are 3 to $5\ \mu m$.
A human RBC is about $7\ \mu m$.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 swap the RBC and Mycoplasma sizes. Bacteria are 3 to $5\ \mu m$, not $0.3\ \mu m$.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the sizes of Mycoplasma and the human RBC.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; plant and animal cells
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Bacterial shapes.
steps: Bacillus is rod-shaped (A-III).
Coccus is spherical (B-I).
Vibrio is comma-shaped (C-II).
Spirillum is spiral (D-IV).
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap bacillus with coccus, or vibrio with spirillum.
solution.common_trap: Confusing vibrio (comma) with spirillum (spiral).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; plant and animal cells
questions.question: Which of the following statements about prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are correct?

statements.A: Plasmids are small circular extrachromosomal DNA that may confer antibiotic resistance.
statements.B: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S, made of 60S and 40S subunits.
statements.C: Prokaryotic cells possess mitochondria but lack endoplasmic reticulum.
statements.D: A polysome consists of several ribosomes attached to a single mRNA.
statements.E: Nerve cells are the largest isolated single cells.

options: A, B, C and D only

solution.key_concept: Features of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
steps: A is correct: plasmids are extrachromosomal and may confer antibiotic resistance.
B is correct: eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S (60S + 40S).
C is wrong: prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles, so they have no mitochondria.
D is correct: several ribosomes on one mRNA form a polysome.
E is wrong: nerve cells are the longest cells, while the ostrich egg is the largest isolated single cell.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 leaves out D. Option 2 includes C. Option 4 includes E and leaves out A.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the longest cell (nerve cell) with the largest isolated cell (ostrich egg).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell envelope, cell membrane and cell wall
questions.question: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by

solution.key_concept: Fluid mosaic model.
steps: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972.
It describes a quasi-fluid lipid bilayer that allows lateral movement of proteins.
solution.why_not_others: Schleiden and Schwann proposed cell theory. Camillo Golgi observed the Golgi apparatus. Virchow proposed Omnis cellula-e cellula.
solution.common_trap: Linking the plasma membrane to Schwann, who only described it in animal cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell envelope, cell membrane and cell wall
questions.question: The middle lamella that holds neighbouring plant cells together is mainly composed of

solution.key_concept: Composition of the plant cell wall layers.
steps: The middle lamella is mainly calcium pectate.
Cellulose and hemicellulose are components of the plant cell wall proper.
Calcium carbonate occurs in algal walls.
solution.why_not_others: Cellulose and hemicellulose belong to the primary and secondary walls. Calcium carbonate is found in algal cell walls.
solution.common_trap: Choosing cellulose because it is the best-known wall component.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell envelope, cell membrane and cell wall
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the bacterial mesosome?
options: DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells

solution.key_concept: Functions of the mesosome.
steps: The mesosome is an extension of the plasma membrane into the cell.
It helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution, respiration and secretion, and it increases membrane surface area.
Motility is the role of flagella, not mesosomes.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1-3 are all listed functions of the mesosome.
solution.common_trap: Thinking every membrane extension also helps the cell move.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell envelope, cell membrane and cell wall
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Pili and fimbriae are the structures responsible for motility in bacteria.
statements.R: A bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts: filament, hook and basal body.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Surface structures of bacteria.
steps: Pili and fimbriae help attachment, not motility, so A is false.
Bacteria move by flagella, which have a filament, a hook and a basal body, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every bacterial surface appendage helps in movement.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell envelope, cell membrane and cell wall
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In the human RBC membrane, protein (about 52%) is present in a greater proportion than lipid (about 40%).
statements.II: The secondary wall of a plant cell is formed on the outer side of the primary wall.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Membrane composition and cell wall layering.
steps: The human RBC membrane has about 52% protein and 40% lipid, so Statement I is correct.
The secondary wall forms on the inner side of the primary wall, towards the membrane, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II reverses the position of the secondary wall, so options 1 and 4 fail. Statement I is true, so options 2 and 4 fail.
solution.common_trap: Assuming lipid exceeds protein in the membrane, or placing the secondary wall outside the primary wall.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endomembrane system: ER, Golgi bodies, lysosomes and vacuoles
questions.question: The membrane that bounds the vacuole in a plant cell is called the

solution.key_concept: Structure of the vacuole.
steps: The vacuole is bounded by a single membrane called the tonoplast.
The tonoplast transports ions into the vacuole against the concentration gradient.
solution.why_not_others: The plasma membrane bounds the whole cell. The middle lamella cements adjacent cell walls. Cisternae are the flat sacs of the Golgi.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the tonoplast with the plasma membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endomembrane system: ER, Golgi bodies, lysosomes and vacuoles
questions.question: In animal cells, steroidal hormones are synthesised in the

solution.key_concept: Functions of SER and RER.
steps: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is the major site of lipid synthesis.
In animal cells, steroidal hormones are lipid-derived and are made in the SER.
solution.why_not_others: RER makes proteins for secretion. The Golgi packages materials and forms glycoproteins. Lysosomes carry out hydrolytic digestion.
solution.common_trap: Choosing RER because hormones are associated with secretion.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endomembrane system: ER, Golgi bodies, lysosomes and vacuoles
questions.question: Which of the following organelles is a part of the endomembrane system?

solution.key_concept: Components of the endomembrane system.
steps: The endomembrane system comprises the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles, whose functions are coordinated.
Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not included.
solution.why_not_others: The mitochondrion, peroxisome and chloroplast are membrane-bound, but their functions are not coordinated with the ER and Golgi.
solution.common_trap: Including every membrane-bound organelle in the endomembrane system.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endomembrane system: ER, Golgi bodies, lysosomes and vacuoles
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Functions of the endomembrane components.
steps: The cis (forming) face of the Golgi receives material from the ER (A-II).
Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases (B-III).
The contractile vacuole of Amoeba carries out osmoregulation and excretion (C-I).
RER is involved in protein synthesis and secretion (D-IV).
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps A and B. Option 2 swaps C and D. Option 4 swaps A and D.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the receiving role of the cis face with the protein-synthesising role of the RER.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endomembrane system: ER, Golgi bodies, lysosomes and vacuoles
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles are correct?

statements.A: The Golgi apparatus is the site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
statements.B: The tonoplast transports ions into the vacuole against the concentration gradient, so the concentration of vacuolar sap exceeds that of the cytoplasm.
statements.C: The trans face of the Golgi is the convex forming face.
statements.D: Lysosomes bud off from the Golgi and contain hydrolases that are optimally active at acidic pH.

solution.key_concept: Structure and function of the Golgi, lysosomes and vacuoles.
steps: A is correct: glycoproteins and glycolipids are formed in the Golgi.
B is correct: the tonoplast pumps ions in against the gradient, which concentrates the sap.
C is wrong: the cis face is the convex forming face, while the trans face is the concave maturing face.
D is correct: lysosomes come from the Golgi and contain acid hydrolases.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 3 include the false statement C. Option 4 leaves out the true statement B.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the cis (convex, forming) and trans (concave, maturing) faces of the Golgi.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitochondria, ribosomes, plastids and microbodies
questions.question: Which type of leucoplast stores oils and fats?

solution.key_concept: Leucoplasts are colourless storage plastids. Each type stores a specific reserve.
steps: Amyloplasts store starch.
Elaioplasts store oils and fats.
Aleuroplasts store proteins.
solution.why_not_others: Amyloplasts store starch and aleuroplasts store proteins. Chromoplasts are pigmented plastids containing carotenoids, not storage leucoplasts.
solution.common_trap: Confusing aleuroplast (protein) with elaioplast (oil) because the names sound similar.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link 'elaio' with oil (as in olive), 'amylo' with starch and 'aleuro' with protein.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitochondria, ribosomes, plastids and microbodies
questions.question: Which feature is common to both mitochondria and chloroplasts?
options: 80S ribosomes like those of the cytoplasm

solution.key_concept: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles.
steps: The mitochondrial matrix contains circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
The chloroplast stroma also contains circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
Both organelles have a double membrane.
solution.why_not_others: Cristae are found only in mitochondria. Both organelles have 70S ribosomes, not 80S. Both are double-membrane bound, not single-membrane bound.
solution.common_trap: Assuming organelle ribosomes are 80S like cytoplasmic ribosomes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitochondria, ribosomes, plastids and microbodies
questions.question: How many chloroplasts are typically present in a leaf mesophyll cell?

solution.key_concept: The number of chloroplasts per cell varies between organisms.
steps: Chlamydomonas has a single chloroplast.
Leaf mesophyll cells have 20 to 40 chloroplasts.
The figures 5 to 10 $\mu m$ and 2 to 4 $\mu m$ are the length and width of a chloroplast, not counts.
solution.why_not_others: 'Only one' describes Chlamydomonas. The values 5 to 10 and 2 to 4 are chloroplast dimensions in $\mu m$, not numbers of chloroplasts.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up chloroplast dimensions with the number of chloroplasts per cell.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitochondria, ribosomes, plastids and microbodies
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell'.
statements.R: The mitochondrial matrix contains circular DNA, a few RNA molecules and 70S ribosomes.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Mitochondria are named the powerhouse because they are the sites of aerobic respiration and ATP production.
steps: A is true: mitochondria produce ATP through aerobic respiration.
R is true: the matrix has circular DNA, RNA and 70S ribosomes.
R explains the semi-autonomous nature of mitochondria, not their role in energy production.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, so options 3 and 4 are ruled out. R does not explain ATP production, so option 1 is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Choosing option 1 simply because both statements describe mitochondria.
solution.time_saving_tip: Ask whether R explains why A happens. Here R describes a different property.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitochondria, ribosomes, plastids and microbodies
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Ribosomes are single-membrane-bound RNA-protein particles that were first observed by George Palade.
statements.II: Microbodies, which include peroxisomes and glyoxysomes, are single-membrane vesicles containing enzymes and occur in both plant and animal cells.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Ribosomes have no membrane, whereas microbodies are bounded by a single membrane.
steps: Ribosomes are non-membranous particles first observed by Palade in 1953, so Statement I is incorrect.
Microbodies are single-membrane vesicles with enzymes and are found in both plant and animal cells, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution.why_not_others: Statement I wrongly gives ribosomes a membrane, which rules out options 1 and 3. Statement II is fully correct, which rules out option 2.
solution.common_trap: Seeing the correct discoverer (Palade) and accepting the whole of Statement I.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella and centrioles
questions.question: Which arrangement of microtubules is found in the axoneme of a eukaryotic cilium?
options: 9+2 (nine peripheral doublets and a central pair)
9+2 (nine peripheral triplets and a central pair)

solution.key_concept: The axoneme has a 9+2 arrangement of microtubules.
steps: The axoneme has nine peripheral doublet microtubules.
It also has a pair of central microtubules enclosed by a central sheath.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 9+2 (nine peripheral doublets and a central pair)
solution.why_not_others: A 9+0 arrangement of triplets describes the centriole. The axoneme peripheral fibrils are doublets, not triplets, and the axoneme does have central tubules.
solution.common_trap: Confusing axoneme doublets with centriole triplets.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella and centrioles
questions.question: In the axoneme of a flagellum, which structure connects each peripheral doublet to the central sheath?

solution.key_concept: Several different connecting structures are found in the 9+2 axoneme.
steps: Each peripheral doublet is joined to the central sheath by a radial spoke.
Linkers join adjacent peripheral doublets.
Bridges join the two central tubules.
solution.why_not_others: Linkers join neighbouring doublets and bridges join the central tubules. The central hub belongs to the cartwheel structure of the centriole, not the axoneme.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up linkers and radial spokes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella and centrioles
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the arrangement of the two centrioles in a centrosome?
options: They lie parallel to each other and are surrounded by a central sheath
They lie parallel to each other and are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar material
They lie perpendicular to each other and are joined to a central sheath by radial spokes
They lie perpendicular to each other and are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar material

solution.key_concept: A centrosome contains two cylindrical centrioles embedded in pericentriolar material.
steps: The two centrioles lie perpendicular to each other.
They are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar material.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): They lie perpendicular to each other and are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar material
solution.why_not_others: The centrioles are not parallel. A central sheath joined to doublets by radial spokes is a feature of the axoneme, not the centrosome.
solution.common_trap: Borrowing axoneme terms such as central sheath and radial spoke to describe the centrosome.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella and centrioles
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Centriole-like structure from which cilia arise

solution.key_concept: This question tests the differences between the axoneme and the centriole.
steps: Axoneme peripheral fibrils are doublets, so A matches I.
Centriole peripheral fibrils are triplets, so B matches II.
The central hub is the proteinaceous core of the cartwheel, so C matches III.
Cilia arise from centriole-like basal bodies, so D matches IV.
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 4 swap doublets and triplets. Options 3 and 4 swap the descriptions of the hub and the basal body.
solution.common_trap: Assigning triplets to the axoneme.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fix A and B first. Only options 1 and 3 have A-I, B-II, and then C decides between them.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella and centrioles
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella and centrioles are correct?

statements.A: The cytoskeleton consists of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments.
statements.B: Each peripheral fibril of a centriole is made of tubulin and is a triplet.
statements.C: Cilia work like oars and are longer than flagella.
statements.D: Centrioles are present in almost all higher plant cells.
statements.E: Prokaryotic flagella differ structurally from eukaryotic flagella.

solution.key_concept: This question tests the components and structure of the cytoskeleton and of microtubule-based organelles.
steps: A is true: the cytoskeleton has three components.
B is true: centriole fibrils are tubulin triplets.
C is false: cilia are small, and it is flagella that are longer.
D is false: centrioles are absent in almost all higher plant cells.
E is true: prokaryotic and eukaryotic flagella differ in structure.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 includes the false statement C. Option 3 includes the false statement D. Option 4 includes C and leaves out the true statement B.
solution.common_trap: Believing centrioles occur in higher plants because spindle fibres form there too.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Nucleus: nuclear membrane, chromatin and nucleolus
questions.question: Who first described the nucleus, in 1831?

solution.key_concept: This question tests the history of nuclear studies.
steps: Robert Brown described the nucleus in 1831.
Flemming later named the stainable material chromatin.
solution.why_not_others: Flemming named chromatin, Palade observed ribosomes, and Schleiden is linked with cell theory.
solution.common_trap: Confusing Flemming's naming of chromatin with the discovery of the nucleus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Nucleus: nuclear membrane, chromatin and nucleolus
questions.question: What is the width of the perinuclear space between the two membranes of the nuclear envelope?

solution.key_concept: The nuclear envelope has two parallel membranes separated by the perinuclear space.
steps: The perinuclear space measures 10 to 50 nm.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 3 are smaller and larger by a factor of ten. The range 0.2 to 1.0 $\mu m$ is the width of a mitochondrion.
solution.common_trap: Recalling the mitochondrial width instead of the perinuclear space.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Nucleus: nuclear membrane, chromatin and nucleolus
questions.question: A chromosome has its centromere located near one end, but not at the very tip. What type of chromosome is it?

solution.key_concept: Chromosomes are classified by the position of the centromere.
steps: Metacentric: the centromere is in the middle.
Sub-metacentric: the centromere is slightly away from the middle.
Acrocentric: the centromere is near the end.
Telocentric: the centromere is terminal.
solution.why_not_others: Metacentric and sub-metacentric chromosomes have the centromere at or near the middle. Telocentric chromosomes have the centromere exactly at the end.
solution.common_trap: Confusing acrocentric (near the end) with telocentric (at the end).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Nucleus: nuclear membrane, chromatin and nucleolus
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Nucleoli are larger and more numerous in cells that are actively carrying out protein synthesis.
statements.R: The nucleolus is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Nucleoli make rRNA, which is needed to build ribosomes for protein synthesis.
steps: A is true, as stated in the notes.
R is true: nucleoli are sites of active rRNA synthesis.
Greater protein synthesis needs more ribosomes and therefore more rRNA, so R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, which rules out options 3 and 4. R directly accounts for A, which rules out option 2.
solution.common_trap: Failing to connect rRNA synthesis with ribosome demand.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Nucleus: nuclear membrane, chromatin and nucleolus
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The outer membrane of the nuclear envelope is usually continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and bears ribosomes.
statements.II: Chromatin contains DNA and RNA together with acidic histone proteins and non-histone proteins.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Histones are basic proteins.
steps: Statement I is correct: the outer nuclear membrane is continuous with the ER and carries ribosomes.
Statement II is incorrect: chromatin contains basic histone proteins, not acidic ones.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II contains the single wrong word 'acidic', which rules out options 1 and 4. Statement I is correct, which rules out option 2.
solution.common_trap: Overlooking the word 'acidic' in a statement that is otherwise correct.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Biomolecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids
questions.question: Inulin is a polymer of which sugar?

solution.key_concept: Polysaccharides differ in their monomer units.
steps: Inulin is a polymer of fructose.
Cellulose and starch are polymers of glucose.
solution.why_not_others: Glucose is the monomer of cellulose and starch. Galactose and ribose are not the monomers of inulin.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every plant polysaccharide is made of glucose.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Biomolecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids
questions.question: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 18% adenine. What is the percentage of guanine in it?

solution.key_concept: Chargaff's rule for double-stranded DNA states that $A = T$ and $G = C$.
solution.why_not_others: 18% wrongly assumes $G = A$. 64% is $G + C$, not G alone. 36% is $A + T$.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting to divide $G + C$ by 2.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Biomolecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids
questions.question: What is the length of a B-DNA molecule containing 2000 base pairs?

solution.key_concept: The length of B-DNA is given by $L = N_{bp} \times 0.34\ nm$.
steps: Check: 2000 bp is 200 turns, and $200 \times 3.4 = 680\ nm$.
solution.why_not_others: 68 nm comes from a decimal-place error. 6800 nm results from using 3.4 nm per base pair. 340 nm results from treating the 2000 bp as 2000 nucleotides, which gives only 1000 bp.
solution.common_trap: Using the pitch of 3.4 nm per turn as the rise per base pair.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Biomolecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Most abundant protein in the animal world

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Most abundant protein in the biosphere

solution.key_concept: This question tests well-known examples of biomolecules.
steps: RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the biosphere, so A matches IV.
Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world, so B matches I.
Lecithin is a phospholipid, so C matches II.
Haemoglobin has quaternary structure with $2\alpha + 2\beta$ subunits, so D matches III.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 4 swap RuBisCO and collagen. Options 3 and 4 swap lecithin and haemoglobin.
solution.common_trap: Calling collagen the most abundant protein overall.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Biomolecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids
questions.question: Which of the following statements about biomolecules are correct?

statements.A: The acid-soluble pool contains micromolecules with molecular weights below 1000 Da.
statements.B: Lipids are absent from the acid-insoluble fraction because they are not polymers.
statements.C: Cellulose holds $I_2$ in its helix and gives a blue colour with iodine.
statements.D: Palmitic acid has 16 carbon atoms, including the carboxyl carbon.
statements.E: A nucleotide is a nucleoside plus a phosphate group.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: This question tests acid-soluble and acid-insoluble fractions, polysaccharide properties, fatty acids and nucleotides.
steps: A is true: acid-soluble molecules are below 1000 Da.
B is false: lipids appear in the acid-insoluble fraction as membrane vesicles.
C is false: starch holds $I_2$, but cellulose does not.
D is true: palmitic acid has 16 carbons, including the carboxyl carbon.
E is true: a nucleotide is a nucleoside plus a phosphate.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, D and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 includes the false statement B. Option 2 includes B and C. Option 4 includes C.
solution.common_trap: Excluding lipids from the acid-insoluble fraction because they are not polymers.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Enzymes: types, properties, action, classification and nomenclature
questions.question: Which metal ion acts as a cofactor for the enzyme carboxypeptidase?

solution.key_concept: Metal ions are one type of enzyme cofactor. Zinc is the cofactor for carboxypeptidase.
steps: Cofactors are of three kinds: prosthetic groups, coenzymes and metal ions.
Carboxypeptidase requires zinc as its metal ion cofactor.
solution.why_not_others: Iron, magnesium and copper are not the cofactor named for carboxypeptidase. Iron is part of haem, the prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase, not a free metal cofactor of carboxypeptidase.
solution.common_trap: Linking the iron of haem with carboxypeptidase. Haem belongs to peroxidase and catalase.
solution.time_saving_tip: Memorise the pairs: haem with peroxidase and catalase, NAD/NADP with niacin, zinc with carboxypeptidase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Enzymes: types, properties, action, classification and nomenclature
questions.question: An enzyme has $V_{max} = 80$ units and $K_m = 4$ mM. Using the Michaelis–Menten relation, what is the reaction velocity when the substrate concentration is 12 mM?

solution.key_concept: Michaelis–Menten relation: $V = \frac{V_{max}[S]}{K_m + [S]}$
steps: Substitute the values: $V = \frac{80 \times 12}{4 + 12}$.
Numerator: $80 \times 12 = 960$. Denominator: $4 + 12 = 16$.
solution.why_not_others: 40 units is $V_{max}/2$, which applies only when $[S] = K_m$. 20 units comes from putting $K_m$ in place of $[S]$ in the numerator. 240 units comes from dividing by $K_m$ alone instead of $(K_m + [S])$.
solution.common_trap: Assuming V always equals $V_{max}/2$, or leaving $[S]$ out of the denominator.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Enzymes: types, properties, action, classification and nomenclature
questions.question: An enzyme removes a group from its substrate by a mechanism other than hydrolysis, and a double bond is formed in the product. To which enzyme class does it belong?

solution.key_concept: Lyases remove groups by non-hydrolytic means, leaving double bonds.
steps: The group is removed without water, so the enzyme is not a hydrolase.
Removing a group to form a double bond is the defining feature of lyases.
solution.why_not_others: Hydrolases break bonds using water. Ligases join two compounds. Isomerases interconvert isomers and do not remove groups.
solution.common_trap: Confusing lyases with ligases because the names sound similar.
solution.time_saving_tip: Lyase means removal without water plus a double bond. Ligase means joining.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Enzymes: types, properties, action, classification and nomenclature
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Enzymes exposed to low temperature are permanently denatured and cannot regain their activity.
statements.R: High temperature destroys enzymatic activity because the enzyme proteins are denatured by heat.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: High temperature denatures enzymes. Low temperature only inactivates them temporarily.
steps: Low temperature causes temporary inactivation, not permanent denaturation, so A is false.
High temperature denatures enzyme proteins and destroys activity, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 need A to be true, but A is false. Option 3 calls R false, but heat denaturation is a correct fact.
solution.common_trap: Treating cold and heat as having the same effect. Cold-inactivated enzymes regain activity when warmed.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Enzymes: types, properties, action, classification and nomenclature
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: A coenzyme is tightly bound to the apoenzyme, whereas a prosthetic group binds to the enzyme only transiently during catalysis.
statements.II: Haem in catalase acts as a prosthetic group, and the coenzyme NAD contains the vitamin niacin.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: A prosthetic group is tightly bound to the enzyme. A coenzyme binds only transiently.
steps: Statement I reverses the definitions, so it is incorrect.
Haem is the prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase, so the first half of Statement II is correct.
NAD and NADP contain niacin, so the second half is also correct. Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 3 accept Statement I, which swaps the binding behaviour of coenzymes and prosthetic groups. Option 2 rejects Statement II, which states correct facts.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the binding nature of coenzymes and prosthetic groups.
solution.time_saving_tip: Prosthetic means permanently attached. A coenzyme comes and goes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell cycle
questions.question: In which phase of the cell cycle does DNA replication take place?

solution.key_concept: The S (synthesis) phase is the phase of DNA replication.
steps: In G1 the cell grows, but its DNA does not replicate.
In S phase DNA replicates, and the DNA content rises from 2C to 4C.
solution.why_not_others: G1 is a growth phase without replication. G2 prepares the cell for mitosis through protein synthesis. M phase is the division phase.
solution.common_trap: Picking G2 because the DNA content is already 4C there. The doubling itself happens in S phase.
solution.time_saving_tip: S stands for synthesis of DNA.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell cycle
questions.question: A diploid cell with chromosome number $2n = 14$ has a DNA content of 2C in G1 phase. What will be its DNA content and chromosome number in G2 phase?

solution.key_concept: S phase doubles the DNA content ($2C \rightarrow 4C$) but leaves the chromosome number unchanged.
steps: DNA replicates during S phase, so the DNA content in G2 becomes 4C.
Each chromosome now has two chromatids, but the number of chromosomes stays 14.
solution.why_not_others: 28 chromosomes wrongly assumes the chromosome number doubles. 2C ignores the DNA replication that occurred in S phase.
solution.common_trap: Assuming S phase doubles the chromosome number.
solution.time_saving_tip: After S phase, only the DNA (C value) doubles, never the n value.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell cycle
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes cells in the G0 stage?
options: They are metabolically inactive and cannot be triggered to divide
They enter G0 directly from the G2 phase
They are actively replicating their DNA
They remain metabolically active but do not proliferate unless triggered

solution.key_concept: G0 is a quiescent stage. Cells exit G1 into G0, stay metabolically active, and can be triggered to divide.
steps: Cells that stop dividing, such as many heart cells, exit G1 into G0.
G0 cells remain metabolically active but do not proliferate unless triggered.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): They remain metabolically active but do not proliferate unless triggered
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 is wrong because G0 cells are active and can be triggered. Option 2 is wrong because entry into G0 is from G1, not G2. Option 3 is wrong because DNA replication occurs in S phase.
solution.common_trap: Equating quiescent with metabolically inactive.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell cycle
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: DNA replication and centriole duplication in animal cells

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Protein synthesis in preparation for mitosis; DNA content 4C

solution.key_concept: Each phase of the cell cycle has a characteristic event.
steps: G1: the cell grows, and DNA stays 2C because it has not yet replicated (III).
S: DNA replicates and the centriole duplicates (II).
G2: protein synthesis continues for mitosis, with DNA at 4C (IV).
G0: a quiescent but metabolically active stage (I).
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 assigns replication to G1. Option 2 swaps G2 and G0. Option 3 swaps G1 and G2, ignoring the 2C and 4C DNA contents.
solution.common_trap: Matching G1 and G2 interchangeably because growth occurs in both. Use the DNA content to tell them apart.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fix S phase first (II); the 2C/4C clue then separates G1 from G2.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cell cycle
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle are correct?

statements.A: Interphase occupies more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.
statements.B: In animals, mitosis can occur in both haploid and diploid cells.
statements.C: Yeast completes its cell cycle in about 90 minutes.
statements.D: Many heart cells exit G1 phase and enter the G0 stage.
statements.E: S phase doubles the chromosome number from 2n to 4n.

options: A, B, C and D only

solution.key_concept: Facts about cell cycle duration, G0 cells and S phase.
steps: A is true: interphase takes more than 95% of the cycle.
B is false: in animals mitosis occurs only in diploid somatic cells. It is in plants that haploid cells can also divide mitotically.
C is true: yeast takes about 90 minutes.
D is true: many heart cells enter G0.
E is false: S phase doubles DNA content (2C to 4C), not chromosome number.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 leaves out the true statement D. Option 2 includes the false statement B. Option 4 includes the false statement E and leaves out A.
solution.common_trap: Applying the plant rule (haploid cells can divide mitotically) to animals.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminate any option containing B or E. Only option 3 remains.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitosis
questions.question: Which stage of mitosis is considered best for studying the morphology of chromosomes?

solution.key_concept: At metaphase, condensed chromosomes align at the metaphase plate.
steps: In metaphase, each chromosome has two sister chromatids and lies at the metaphase plate.
This makes metaphase the best stage for studying chromosome morphology.
solution.why_not_others: In prophase condensation is still in progress. In anaphase the chromatids are moving apart. In telophase the chromosomes decondense.
solution.common_trap: Choosing prophase because chromosomes first become visible then.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitosis
questions.question: A single cell undergoes 5 successive mitotic divisions. How many cells will be formed?

solution.key_concept: The number of cells after n mitotic divisions is $N = 2^n$.
steps: Here $n = 5$.
solution.why_not_others: 10 comes from multiplying $2 \times 5$. 25 comes from calculating $5^2$. 64 is $2^6$, which counts one division too many.
solution.common_trap: Multiplying instead of raising 2 to the power n.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitosis
questions.question: When karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, a multinucleate condition called a syncytium is formed. Which of the following is an example of a syncytium?
options: Cell plate of a dividing plant cell
Meristematic cells of the shoot apex
Heart cells in the G0 stage

solution.key_concept: A syncytium results from nuclear division without cytoplasmic division.
steps: Repeated karyokinesis without cytokinesis gives one cytoplasm containing many nuclei.
The liquid endosperm of coconut is the classic example.
solution.why_not_others: The cell plate is a structure formed during plant cytokinesis, not a multinucleate cell. Meristematic cells divide normally, completing cytokinesis. G0 heart cells are non-dividing.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the cell plate (cytokinesis) with the syncytium (absence of cytokinesis).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitosis
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.R: Mitosis helps in maintaining the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio of cells.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Mitosis is equational because the daughter cells have the same chromosome number as the parent cell.
steps: A is true: mitosis is equational division.
R is true: mitosis restores the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
The term 'equational' refers to the chromosome number staying equal, not to the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio, so R does not explain A.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 wrongly links the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio to the term 'equational'. Options 3 and 4 each deny a statement that is true.
solution.common_trap: Accepting any true significance of mitosis as the explanation for its name.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mitosis
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: By the end of prophase, the Golgi complex, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and nuclear envelope are no longer visible.
statements.II: In plants, both haploid and diploid cells can divide by mitosis, whereas in animals mitosis occurs only in diploid somatic cells.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Events at the end of prophase, and which cells can divide by mitosis.
steps: Statement I is correct: at the end of prophase the Golgi, ER, nucleolus and nuclear envelope are not seen. They reform in telophase.
Statement II is correct: plant cells divide mitotically as n → n or 2n → 2n, while in animals mitosis occurs only in diploid somatic cells.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Every other option marks a correct statement as incorrect.
solution.common_trap: Thinking the nuclear envelope disappears only in metaphase, or that haploid cells can never divide by mitosis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Meiosis and its significance
questions.question: In which sub-stage of prophase I does crossing over occur?

solution.key_concept: Crossing over occurs in pachytene at recombination nodules, with the help of recombinase.
steps: Zygotene is the stage of synapsis.
Pachytene is the stage of crossing over.
Diplotene is when chiasmata become visible.
solution.why_not_others: In leptotene chromosomes only become visible. Zygotene is synapsis. In diplotene the chiasmata, which result from crossing over, become visible.
solution.common_trap: Placing crossing over in zygotene or diplotene.
solution.time_saving_tip: Memorise the order L-Z-P-D-D: visible, pair, cross, chiasmata, terminalise.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Meiosis and its significance
questions.question: How many meiotic divisions are needed to produce 100 haploid cells, given that each meiosis yields four haploid cells?

solution.key_concept: One meiosis gives $2n \rightarrow 4 \times n$, that is, four haploid cells.
steps: Number of meioses = number of haploid cells ÷ 4.
solution.why_not_others: 100 assumes one cell per meiosis. 50 assumes two cells per meiosis, as in mitosis. 200 multiplies by 2 instead of dividing by 4.
solution.common_trap: Dividing by 2 as for mitosis instead of by 4.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Meiosis and its significance
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes anaphase I from anaphase II of meiosis?
options: Sister chromatids separate in anaphase I, while homologous chromosomes separate in anaphase II
Sister chromatids separate in both anaphase I and anaphase II
Homologous chromosomes separate in anaphase I, while sister chromatids separate in anaphase II
DNA replicates before anaphase II during interkinesis, but not before anaphase I

solution.key_concept: Anaphase I is reductional (homologues separate). Anaphase II separates sister chromatids, as in mitosis.
steps: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together.
In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Homologous chromosomes separate in anaphase I, while sister chromatids separate in anaphase II
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 reverses the events. Option 2 ignores the separation of homologues in anaphase I. Option 4 is wrong because interkinesis has no DNA replication.
solution.common_trap: Thinking meiosis I resembles mitosis. It is meiosis II that resembles mitosis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Meiosis and its significance
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Dissolution of synaptonemal complex and appearance of chiasmata

solution.key_concept: Each sub-stage of prophase I has a characteristic event.
steps: Leptotene: chromosomes become visible (III).
Zygotene: synapsis through the synaptonemal complex (IV).
Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata appear (II).
Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalise (I).
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps leptotene and zygotene. Option 2 swaps diplotene and diakinesis. Option 3 swaps zygotene and diplotene.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the appearance of chiasmata (diplotene) with their terminalisation (diakinesis).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Meiosis and its significance
questions.question: Which of the following statements about meiosis are correct?

statements.A: Meiosis involves two rounds of DNA replication followed by two divisions.
statements.B: Interkinesis is short and is not accompanied by DNA replication.
statements.C: In oocytes, diplotene can last for months or years.
statements.E: Recombinase acts during zygotene to form bivalents.

options: B, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Meiosis has a single round of DNA replication followed by two divisions.
steps: A is false: there is only one round of DNA replication.
B is true: interkinesis is short and has no DNA replication.
C is true: diplotene is long-lasting in oocytes.
D is true: meiosis II resembles mitosis.
E is false: recombinase acts in pachytene during crossing over, while zygotene is synapsis.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): B, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 leaves out the true statement C. Option 2 includes the false statement A. Option 4 includes the false statement E.
solution.common_trap: Assigning recombinase or crossing over to zygotene.
solution.time_saving_tip: Reject options containing A or E. Of the rest, only option 3 includes all of B, C and D.
